title: Marketplace verification flow and customer copy sketch
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft that combines the technical readiness gates we require for cloud marketplace listings (AWS/Azure/GCP) with succinct, customer-facing copy variants to be validated by legal and product. Goal is a single preflight runbook for Partner Ops + Marketplace PMs to use when shepherding a partner or internal listing to publication.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Partner Ops, Marketplace PM, Solutions Engineering, Legal, Billing/Sales Ops.
- Scope: Hosted product listings (SaaS) and publisher-managed AMIs/VM images where Redwood provides managed inference endpoints. Not covering ISV containers or Marketplace SaaS with embedded installation guides in detail.

High-level verification flow (recommended):
1) Intake & eligibility (Partner Ops)
   - Validate partner identity, MSA status, basic contact matrix.
   - Confirm targeted clouds & regions.
   - Tie to account owner and handoff Jira ticket.
2) Technical gating (Solutions Eng + Infra)
   - Confirm network access model (public API, VPC peering, PrivateLink).
   - Verify auth model: OAuth client + token exchange or API key flow. If SSO required, list SCIM/SAML config sample.
   - KMS & secrets: confirm whether partner will use Redwood KMS integrations or customer-managed KMS — collect key IDs and policy owner.
   - Logging & telemetry: Confirm audit log retention, endpoint logging endpoints (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Monitor), and required redaction rules.
3) Compliance & legal (Legal + Security)
   - Complete marketplace security questionnaire, attach pen-test summary if required.
   - Confirm data handling statements for PII and regulatory controls (HIPAA/GDPR/CCPA as applicable).
4) Billing & SKU mapping (Billing Ops)
   - Create SKU mapping doc: internal sku -> marketplace sku -> plan tiers.
   - Validate pricing tile text and metering dimensions (per-token units, inference-requests, embedding-units).
5) Copy review & creative assets (Marketing + Marketplace PM)
   - Finalize listing descriptions, short pitch, screenshots, and 3 accepted screenshots/video thumbnails.
6) Preflight QA & publish (Partner Ops + Marketplace PM)\   - Run publish dry-run, QA in sandbox listing, verify telemetry, billing flows, and subscription lifecycle.

Technical checklist (detailed):
- API surface:
  - Public endpoint hostnames for each region (list sample).
  - Supported models & versioning policy note (how we represent pinning in the listing).
  - Rate limits and soft/hard quotas example.
- Authentication:
  - OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow sample + token refresh TTLs.
  - API key creation UI path if applicable; rotation policy.
- Network/topology:
  - PrivateLink/EndpointService ARN (if applicable).
  - VPC peering acceptance window & route table steps.
- Identity provisioning:
  - SCIM endpoint + sample attribute map (email, name, teams).
  - SAML metadata file or IdP config snippets.
- Security & compliance artifacts:
  - SOC2 summary (if available), ISO certs, pen test 3rd-party report link or stub.
  - DLP redaction rules and retention settings (max 90 days default).
- Observability & SLOs:
  - Expected 95/99 latency SLOs for common payload sizes.
  - Logging endpoints and example trace IDs for QA.
- Billing tests:
  - Test subscription purchase flow checklist and sample invoice snapshot.
  - Metering snapshot for a small workload (1000 tokens) and expected charge.

Pre-flight runbook (step-by-step):
1) Create Jira GTMP ticket with all artifacts attached (copy, images, SLA PDF, SKU mapping, security questionnaire).
2) Solutions Eng to run the smoke script against staging endpoints (script link in linked artifacts).
3) Security to verify the security questionnaire and sign-off.
4) Billing to confirm SKU creation and test purchase.
5) Marketing to validate final listing copy and creatives.
6) Marketplace PM to schedule publish window and notify partners.

Customer-facing copy sketches (short + long variants). Pick tone: technical, pragmatic, approachable.
- Short (60 char): "Fast, cost-efficient LLM inference—hosted across AWS, Azure, GCP."
- Medium (1-line): "Redwood Inference: predictable latency and cost for production LLMs, with dedicated and private deployment options."
- Long (listing tile ~300 words):
  "Run large language models in production with predictable performance and transparent economics. Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime for hosted APIs, dedicated GPU pools, and private deployments so your team can ship LLM features without building inference infrastructure. Features include: streaming generation, model version pinning, intelligent batching and caching, and built-in rollouts and fallbacks. Integrates with cloud logging, KMS, and SSO; supports per-request observability and per-token billing. Ideal for product teams building chat, summarization, or embeddings at scale."

Copy variants for tile/description to A/B test (examples):
- Variant A: emphasize cost: "Lower per-token cost with intelligent batching and cache-aware execution. Use Redwood to reduce inference bill while keeping latency."
- Variant B: emphasize reliability: "SLA-backed endpoints, multi-region failover, and automatic fallbacks keep your LLM features online under load."
- Variant C: emphasize compliance: "Private deployments and KMS integrations for regulated workloads—HIPAA and enterprise-ready controls."

Acceptance criteria (must be met before publish):
- All technical checklist items addressed and documented in Jira.
- Legal and security sign-offs present and dated.
- Billing SKU validated and end-to-end test purchase passed.
- All creatives sized correctly and uploaded to marketplace asset store.
- Short and long copy variants reviewed by product marketing and legal.

Open questions / risks:
- Do we require a separate privacy addendum for each marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP)? (Action: Legal)
- Billing meter differences between vendors (meter granularity) may require micro-pricing variants. (Action: Billing Ops)
- Region-limited models and model-version pin compatibility across clouds—need canonical table. (Action: Applied ML)

Next steps & owners:
- Aisha (Partner Ops): collect final legal artifacts by 2026-02-28.
- Marco (Solutions Eng): provide sample SCIM and PrivateLink snippets by 2026-02-23.
- Leah (Marketplace PM): schedule sandbox publish run on 2026-03-02.
- Samir (Billing Ops): create SKU draft and test purchase by 2026-02-26.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; if teams want modular expanded sections (detailed SCIM map, sample token exchange flows, or region model matrix) we should create companion sub-docs rather than lengthen this master preflight doc.
- For internal use only: placeholder SLA and certs references must be replaced with final attachments prior to publish.
